top.title: Football roundup: DeWitt adds to streak, Ithaca and P-W set up rematch
top.description: DEWITT 54, COOPERSVILLE 21 DEWITT — Griffin Braman ran for 129 yards and two touchdowns and threw for 63 yards and three touchdowns while helping the Panthers to a Division 3 district final win over Coopersville. Landon Kurncz added three catches for 47 yards and two touchdowns and Joseph Bobeda ran for 87 yards and a touchdown to help DeWitt win a third straight district title. The Panthers advance to face Mount Pleasant next week in a regional final in what is a rematch of last year's Division 3 state title game. PEWAMO-WESTPHALIA 41, ELKTON PIGEON-BAY PORT LAKER 7 WESTPHALIA — Caleb Blyth, Alex Nurenberg and Carter Thelen rushed for touchdowns and Alex Drysdale had a TD reception while contributing to the Pirates capturing a Division 7 district title with a win over Elkton-Pigeon-Bay Port Laker. Pewamo-Westphalia advances to face Ithaca in a regional final next week. ITHACA 39, MILLINGTON 16 MILLINGTON — Gibson Rondy completed 18-of-28 passes for 183 yards and a touchdown and ran for 144 yards and a score to help the Yellowjackets to a victory over Millington in a Division 7 district final. Devyn Fisher had six catches for 91 yards and a TD, the Yellowjackets returned a fumble for a score and Landon Bratschi made a 30-yard field for Ithaca (10-1). The Yellowjackets will face Pewamo-Westphalia next week in a regional final. GOODRICH 49, ST. JOHNS 7 GOODRICH — Conner Kurncz threw for 100 yards and Archer Gurski had a rushing score for the Redwings in their loss to Goodrich in a Division 4 district final. Goodrich jumped out to a 28-0 lead in the second quarter before Gurski scored the lone touchdown for St. Johns, which closes its season with an 8-3 record. top.title: Outside shooting freezes out Michigan basketball in UConn rematch
top.description: BOSTON −The game didn’t matter nearly as much as the last time the two teams met, but the atmosphere was rocking for a November basketball game. Michigan basketball and UConn gave a capacity TD Garden crowd their money’s worth in a national championship game rematch seven months to the day. This time, however, the Huskies prevailed in an 85-77 victory, fueled by an 18-4 run covering the end of the first half and the first four minutes of the second half. U-M’s offense was stagnant much of the evening, shooting just 26-for-63 (41.3%) from the floor and 7-for-28 (25%) from 3. U-M made one shot outside the paint in the first half and didn’t get its second until Quinn Costello hit a corner 3 with 15:39 left. The game flipped late in the first half when UConn, up 32-27, was called for a loose ball foul and its bench was assessed a technical foul for letting the refs hear its displeasure. Trey McKenney missed both free throws for the tech, bringing the fervent UConn crowd to its feet, and J.P. Estrella missed his first before finally giving the Wolverines one make in four tries. U-M and UConn exchanged baskets before the Huskies ripped off a 9-0 run in 2:12 to close the half up by 13. In the second half, they led by nine or more until the final 18 seconds, when U-M cut it to eight. McKenney, who missed his first eight shots, including all seven in the first half, got hot in the second and finished with a team-high 22 points as U-M cut its 18-point deficit in half. But with Elliot Cadeau and Moustapha Thiam on the bench much of the second half with four fouls apiece, there wasn’t enough offense around him. Estrella, the Tennessee transfer in his second game with U-M, impressed again with 19 points and nine rebounds, and fifth-year vet Roddy Gayle Jr. kept U-M hanging around early while finishing with 16 points. But coach Mike Boynton Jr.'s bench went 2-for-12 from the floor and combined for just eight points. Four of those came on consecutive free throws by Mullins, after the U-M bench was assessed a technical foul. top.title: Daddy Showkey: Vanguard Award will be the biggest of my lifetime
top.description: By Clifford Ndujihe & Benjamin Njoku Chief John Odafe Asiemo, 57, popularly known as Daddy Showkey, is a household name in Nigerian music scene. He is the creator of ‘Galala’ music, which sound helped define Nigeria’s street music in the 90s. Read Also: Nostalgia, glitz as icons reunite for Daddy Showkey’s 50th anniversary celebration Daddy Showkey is a nominee for Vanguard Newspaper’s 2026 Entertainment Icon of the year award. Speaking with ululation after being presented with the letter of nomination, on Tuesday at his Lagos residence, he said: “They say a prophet is not recognised by his own people. But I am a prophet who is being recognised by the people who built me. This is the greatest awards I have ever received in my life because it is coming from Vanguard. Vanguard is the first newspaper in Nigeria that wrote about me, when I was nothing. This is Vanguard, and I cherish it a lot. “Apart from that, Vanguard played a big role in pushing me to the limelight. “So, a recognition award coming from Vanguard, I must cherish it. It is like my own people saying it is high time. Sometimes, when I see Vanguard giving people awards, I always say in my mind, when is it going to be my turn? “Now, it is my turn to receive the award and I am very grateful.” Reminiscing on his early days, Daddy Showkey, who celebrated 50 years on the stage recently, continued: “For years, I kept coming to Vanguard head office, but I never met the publisher, Uncle Sam, in person. After my secondary education, I hit the streets. From childhood, I had made up my mind to follow music. At 13, in 1983, I started following Danladi Bako of NTA. I was always at his office on Lagos Island. He would give me a voucher to go and eat, and made me comfortable in his office. My first song, “Big Belle”, was released in 1990 in Nawfia, Njikoka, Enugu-Ukwu, Anambra State. I cannot forget the late Amadi Ogbonna(former Vanguard Entertainment Editor). He was one of the earliest journalists to write about me and played a huge role in my career. Before Ogbonnaya wrote about me, we used to walk from Kirikiri to Olodi areas, passing Vanguard. I remember saying one day while walking past Vanguard ‘this newspaper will one day write about me.’ It came to pass when Ogbonnaya wrote about me for the first time. The second was Smart Irewudo, a former Champion Newspaper reporter, now based in the United States. Before I started recording, during the June 12 crisis, I led Ajegunle boys who blocked roads and extorted money from motorists. Smart took my picture and published it in the Daily Champion. In his mind, he thought he had done me a great favour. He didn’t know the police would come after me. Luckily, one of the policemen from Area F showed my picture to Amadi Ogbonna. He recognised me immediately and called me. When I showed up, Ogbonna took me to the police station and told them I wasn’t a bad boy, they should release me and focus on arresting real criminals. top.description: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 06: Trey McKenney #1 of the Michigan Wolverines drives to the basket against Silas Demary Jr. #5 of the UConn Huskies during the first half at The TD Garden on November 06, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Brian Fluharty/Getty Images) | Getty Images The No. 16 Michigan Wolverines fell 85-77 to the No. 4 UConn Huskies in a national title game rematch on Friday. Michigan fought back after trailing by double digits at halftime, but it wasn’t enough to defeat UConn this time around. Here’s the recap, highlights and stats. Final pic.twitter.com/S2SI407AN8 — Michigan Men's Basketball (@umichbball) November 7, 2026 FIRST HALF Michigan wasted no time getting on the scoreboard as guard Elliot Cadeau found center Moustapha Thiam for an alley-oop slam just seconds into the game. UConn immediately answered with a 7-0 run to take an early lead, though. Michigan went scoreless for over four minutes as UConn went on a 13-3 run to close the half, turning a back-and-forth affair into a 43-30 lead at halftime. top.title: Former Colts All-Pro OG Quenton Nelson to undergo cleanup surgery and will miss at least a few weeks
top.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Quenton Nelson #53 of the Seattle Seahawks in action against the Chicago Bears at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former Indianapolis Colts All-Pro offensive guard Quenton Nelson, who was traded last week to the Seattle Seahawks for a 2027 3rd round pick and 2028 fifth round pick, will undergo minor cleanup cartilage surgery on his balky knee and miss at least a few weeks—although he’ll not be placed on injured reserve at this time: #Seahawks G Quenton Nelson will have surgery to clean out some cartilage in his knee, sources say, as fragments had been causing an issue recently. The plan is for Nelson to avoid Injured Reserve, and his timeline is a few weeks. Seattle has two games, then a Week 11 bye. pic.twitter.com/AZyUFzg7Kj — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 6, 2026 The Seahawks have two games and then their BYE week, so the hopeful expectation for Seattle must be that Nelson could be ready in 3 weeks’ time as opposed to the minimum 4-game period of inactivity that any stint on injured reserve requires before any ensuing activation. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald indicated that Nelson had the knee condition prior to arriving in Seattle via trade, having suffered it in on the road in Week 7 against the Minnesota Vikings while still formerly a member of the Colts. However, he aggravated the knee injury further, during the Seahawks’ 34-17 Monday Night home loss against the Chicago Bears. It’s unfortunate timing for the playoff hopeful Seahawks and Nelson, who was rather unsurprisingly very impressive during his Seahawks debut on primetime . The future Hall-of-Famer figured to be a ‘plug-and-play’ elite left guard for Seattle in no time and didn’t skip a beat during his Pacific Northwest debut. What is interesting is that it seems as though both the Colts and the Seahawks knew of Nelson’s initial knee condition, which likely came up in his physical. Although to be fair, it worsened this past Monday Night. Perhaps that may have been some of interim GM Ed Dodds’ eagerness and motivation in moving Nelson well before the trade deadline, knowing that his knee condition could eventually lead to the perennial All-Pro and pending NFL free agent missing games down the road in 2026. It’s hard to say for sure at this time. Nelson has been incredibly durable in his Canton-bound NFL career to-date, having only missed 4 starts—all of which occurred during the 2021 campaign with the Colts. We wish Big Q a speedy recovery the rest of the way.

top.title: Police rescue 10 stolen children in Abia
top.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—The Abia State Police Command has arrested suspects linked to the October 17 attack on Uratta Divisional Police Headquarters, rescued 10 stolen children and recovered 15 firearms and 30 stolen vehicles in a major security crackdown across the state. The Command also disclosed that it arrested 109 suspects, comprising 89 males and 20 females, in connection with 211 criminal cases recorded between September 11, 2026 and November 6, 2026. Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Afolabi, who disclosed this on Friday while presenting the Command’s operational scorecard, said the arrests followed intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies. On the Uratta police station attack, Afolabi said investigations had led to the arrest of some of the suspected attackers, with one of them allegedly confessing to leading the gang that carried out the assault. He said investigations were ongoing to track down other accomplices and establish the full circumstances surrounding the attack. In a related security operation, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit raided a location at Ubakala, Umuahia South Local Government Area, on October 25, arresting a suspect identified as Osita. The police reportedly recovered two locally fabricated guns, 16 live cartridges and four expended cartridges from the suspect. Another suspect, 30-year-old suspect, was subsequently arrested for allegedly supplying ammunition illegally. Both suspects have been charged to court, according to the CP. On child trafficking, Afolabi said police operatives rescued 10 children during the period under review and reunited them with their families. He specifically disclosed that two suspects, including a 38-year-old , were arrested on October 11 over the alleged stealing of two children, seven-year-old Chiamaka Chikeze and nine-month-old Goodluck Chikeze. The children were reportedly recovered and handed back to their parents, while the suspects were charged to court. The police boss also announced the arrest of a five-man vehicle theft syndicate, aged 43, and 40. A Toyota Corolla with registration number ROU 9338J was recovered from the suspects, who have also been charged to court. In another operation, two suspected cultists, aged 27, and 25, were arrested on October 31 for allegedly dispossessing students of Abia State University, Uturu, of their mobile phones and other valuables at gunpoint. A locally fabricated firearm was recovered from them. The CP said one of the suspects had confessed to belonging to the Black Axe Confraternity, adding that efforts were ongoing to apprehend other members of the gang. top.title: Sean Wesolek cements his place in the Hope post, following 'older brothers'
top.description: HOLLAND - The Hope College men's basketball team has a good blend in the post. Orion Yant is long and lanky, Kyle Blauch is big and strong, then off the bench, Sean Wesolek is in between - and can shoot. Wesolek, a sophomore center, saw time last season, but will be relied upon for much more. He had the best game of his career in Hope's 90-63 season opening win over Anderson (Ind.) on Friday, Nov. 6, at DeVos Fieldhouse. Wesolek totaled 10 points and grabbed three rebounds in 13 key minutes off the bench. "He is a good combination of the two. It is huge because he gets rewarded for doing things the right way," Hope coach Greg Mitchell said. "All he wanted to do last year was learn. He hung out with Kyle and Orion and just soaked it all up. His attitude and charisma allow him to find his potential. He will be ready every game because he has so much respect for the guys before him, which is really cool." More: 'Two-headed monster' on point for Hope College women's basketball this season The 6-foot, 6-inch Bay City native scored four baskets in the paint and nailed a 3-pointer that keyed a run to put the Flying Dutch up double digits - something they didn't relinquish. "I definitely tried to get bigger this offseason. I gained 15 pounds. But I have two bigs in front of me that support me. When I do well, I feel more loved on than anybody," Wesolek said. "That is the difference between Hope and other places. We have guys who will love and support you no matter what." The post trio helped Hope grab 58 rebounds - 29 more than Anderson. Blauch had 13, including five on the offensive end. Yant had nine to go along with 14 points and two blocks. "It is so fun. We are like three brothers. I like to think of them as my older brothers. They took me in last year and it has been great," said Wesolek, whose older sister was an NCAA qualifier and captain for Hope swimming. "Our dynamic has been great. We each do different things well, and I think it is really unique to have that in a post." The guards played well for Hope, too, as Brandon Cargill totaled 20 points, four rebounds and two assists, while Avery Sanchez had 11 points, five rebounds and two assists. "We played really hard. It wasn't super clean. But we rebounded the heck our of it. Our biggest concern is if we are able to rebound. These guys listened," Mitchell said. "We are deep and we play hard. It is a really cohesive group … and we have to keep it rolling. We don't have any seniors but these guys have some big dreams and we have prove it every night." top.title: Windthorst QB Brock Belcher climbs to No. 3 on Texas all-time passing TD list
top.description: Windthorst senior quarterback Brock Belcher added another milestone to his record-setting career Friday, Nov. 6, moving into third place on Texas high school football's all-time passing touchdowns list across all classifications. Belcher threw three touchdown passes in the Trojans' 55-6 victory over Munday, bringing his career total to 168 and moving him past former Ennis quarterback Graham Harrell, who finished with 167. More: QB Cooper Corley's growth as leader fueling Graham football's playoff hopes More: No. 24 Midwestern State football looks to make a playoff push More: Photos of Windthorst vs. Munday high school football The senior entered the game with 38 touchdown passes this season and added scoring throws to three different receivers as Windthorst (9-1, 6-0) closed out the regular season with another dominant performance. Belcher completed 15 of 24 passes for 209 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. He also rushed six times for 49 yards and a touchdown, accounting for four scores in the victory. His first touchdown pass went to Ruben Willden for 30 yards in the opening quarter. Belcher later connected with Aiden Stark for a 15-yard score in the second quarter before finding Brodie Belz for a 21-yard touchdown in the third. The performance continued an impressive senior campaign for Belcher, who has now thrown 41 touchdown passes this season after recording 37 in 2024. Belcher trails only Refugio's Travis Quintanilla (186) and Sunray's Armando Lujan (171) on the UIL-era career passing touchdowns list maintained by Texas High School Football History. top.title: Crash Of The Titans: RV Marquette 93, Detroit Mercy 32
top.description: No one has published photos from the McGuire Center yet, so here’s Alex Egbuonu trying to end some poor guy from Mercyhurst. | Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I don’t think there’s a lot of point in recapping Marquette’s 93-32 victory over Detroit Mercy on Friday night. It’s the second largest margin of victory in program history, trailing only a 67 point victory over Ripon on December 4, 1951. It’s the only 60+ margin of victory game against a team that’s currently in Division 1, and it’s just the second time that Marquette cleared 50+ as a margin since the 2001-02 season. Marquette set a KenPom era record for best defensive efficiency, surrendering just 0.475 points per possession. So, let’s just rattle off the runs that Marquette went on in this game. 6-0 10-0 to lead by 11 7-0 to lead by 15 9-0 to end the half up 22 Combine the last two for 16-2 over the final eight minutes of the first half. 7-0 to start the second half and lead by 29 Combine the last three for 23-2 5-0, and that’s 28-2 over a 14 minute stretch bridging halftime, Marquette by 32 15-0 to lead by 44 9-0 to lead by 51 Combine the last two for 24-2 in less than seven minutes 9-0 to lead by 58 Combine the last three for 33-4 in just under 10 minutes of game time And a nice little 5-0 over the final 1:42 to end the game. How about some stats! top.title: ‘Sort out your internal mess’, APC tells Atiku, ADC after court judgment
top.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The All Progressives Congress APC has told the Senator David Mark-led faction of the African Democratic Congress ADC to go sort out its internal mess and quit its “senseless rants” after a Federal High Court judgment sacked the faction’s leadership. Read Also: ADC Crisis: What becomes of Atiku, Mark, Gombe if Supreme Court decides party’s fate? In a statement Friday in Abuja, the APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, said the ruling party had no hand in the case. “To be clear, APC is neither a party nor an interlocutor in the matter. Nothing about the case has anything to do with the APC. And the APC has absolutely no role in the party’s judicial quagmire,” he said. The judgment, delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, sacked the David Mark-led leadership of the ADC. It also nullified all official acts of that leadership, including its primary election processes and outcomes, like the presidential candidacy of former vice president Atiku Abubakar. Morka said the case was brought by ADC national officers against the faction now removed from office, describing the suit as “a notorious case initiated by leaders of ADC against pirate leaders of ADC.” He accused Mark and his associates of taking over the party “to satisfy Atiku Abubakar’s quixotic presidential ambition.” According to him, “it didn’t matter to them that their hostile takeover of that party was in flagrant violation of the rule of law and ADC’s internal democracy, as a court of competent jurisdiction has now declared.” The APC spokesman also accused the ADC of reacting to court decisions according to whether they favour it. “Every time a court decides against the Senator David Mark-led factional African Democratic Congress, they accuse the All Progressives Congress of collusion and deprecate the judiciary. Every time a court decides in their favour, they hail the rule of law and extol the judiciary,” he said. top.title: Gophers hold off late Tommie push, down St. Thomas 76-62
top.description: Isaac Asuma led all scorers with 20 points in a win over St. Thomas. University of St. Thomas leadership, alums and Patrick Reusse finally got their wish with a Minnesota/St. Thomas regular season contest, in an early-season tilt between the Twin Cities’s two Division I basketball programs. A matchup that hadn’t been revisited in almost 100 years, Minnesota finally relented and hosted the Tommies in what has surely been circled on UST’s calendar for months. And why not? The Tommie roster is chock full of metro kids who weren’t recruited by the Gophers and saw it as a chance to slay the state’s Goliath. It looked like it might be over early, with the Gophers racing out to a double-digit lead thanks to relentless defense and hot shooting from Isaac Asuma. Minnesota pushed that to a 20-point lead late in the half before going to the locker room with a 40-22 lead, holding the Tommies to just 23% shooting. The second half would be a different story, as St. Thomas clearly adjusted to make the Gophers work a little harder on defense, routinely finding seams and wide open looks on sloppy Minnesota rotations. Timely threes, a bevy of Gopher turnovers and easy missed shots opened the door for the Tommies to storm back into the game, cutting the lead to seven on multiple occasions. Minnesota bent but didn’t break, getting to the line effectively and doing just enough to stymie the St. Thomas comeback down the stretch, while walking away with a 76-62 victory and a 2-0 start to the season. It got a little hairy, but Minnesota’s size and strength advantage ultimately gave them a lot of room for error. THE STAT : Isaac Asuma led all scorers with 20 points. He hit four three-pointers in the first half, en route to 14 points. TURNING POINT : Minnesota went on a 16-0 run midway through the first half to push the lead to 17 at the time. This would provide enough cushion to largely coast through the second half and endure multiple St. Thomas runs. HOT : The Gophers were excellent from the free throw line and hit timely FTs when needed, going 19-22 from the line and halting Tommie momentum more than once. NOT : Bobby Durkin was largely MIA on offense and defense, going 1-6 from the field while scoring only five points. NOTABLE : With Kai Shinholster shelved for a month with a calf injury, Orono HS grad Nolan Groves served as the sixth man, playing 29 minutes off the bench and racking up 15 points. He looked good. DID YOU KNOW: Minnesota paid St. Thomas $100,000 for this game, though it is not expected to be a regular occurrence. Not surprising given that Minnesota gets nothing out of the deal other than the opportunity to potentially build the brand of a rival Division I program in its own backyard. UP NEXT : The Gophers hit the road and face Cincinnati on Monday for a true road game against a power conference opponent. It will be a good early-season barometer as the Bearcats, 2-0, are a similarly ranked KenPom team.

top.title: Celtics destroy struggling Hornets, 119-80, in wire-to-wire win
top.description: The Boston Celtics showed a struggling, shorthanded Charlotte Hornets squad no mercy on Friday night. The Green Team went up by as many as 46 points and ultimately prevailed 119-80 at the Spectrum Center, improving to 7-2 on the season and 2-0 in NBA Cup action. The blitz began almost immediately, as the Celtics jumped out to a 20-point lead in the first quarter and led by 31 points at halftime. The C's drained 17 triples in that first half, tying a franchise record, and ended up shooting 54.5 from deep in the lopsided win. Meanwhile, the Hornets shot 22 percent from beyond the arc and an astonishingly abysmal 29.3 percent from the floor. Simply put, the Celtics dominated every aspect of the game. They won the rebounding battle (51-43), doubled up the Hornets on blocks (8-4), and recorded a season-high 33 assists. And while the Hornets were without guard Kon Knueppel, point guard Dennis Schröder, center Moussa Diabaté, and forward Grant Williams due to injury, they never put up much of a fight — especially once forward Brandon Miller left the contest in the second quarter with groin soreness. Charlotte now finds itself on a six-game losing streak and at the bottom of the East Group C standings. Conversely, Boston is at the top of the East Group C standings with a massive point differential and has a great shot at advancing past the group stage of the NBA Cup. top.description: BOSTON — It seemed like the Wolverines were walking into a lion’s den. A motivated UConn team that was out for revenge. A rowdy crowd that was buzzing from start to finish. An essential true road game at a neutral site. nigeria.title: Police rescue 10 stolen children in Abia
nigeria.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—The Abia State Police Command has arrested suspects linked to the October 17 attack on Uratta Divisional Police Headquarters, rescued 10 stolen children and recovered 15 firearms and 30 stolen vehicles in a major security crackdown across the state. The Command also disclosed that it arrested 109 suspects, comprising 89 males and 20 females, in connection with 211 criminal cases recorded between September 11, 2026 and November 6, 2026. Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Afolabi, who disclosed this on Friday while presenting the Command’s operational scorecard, said the arrests followed intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies. On the Uratta police station attack, Afolabi said investigations had led to the arrest of some of the suspected attackers, with one of them allegedly confessing to leading the gang that carried out the assault. He said investigations were ongoing to track down other accomplices and establish the full circumstances surrounding the attack. In a related security operation, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit raided a location at Ubakala, Umuahia South Local Government Area, on October 25, arresting a suspect identified as Osita. The police reportedly recovered two locally fabricated guns, 16 live cartridges and four expended cartridges from the suspect. Another suspect, 30-year-old suspect, was subsequently arrested for allegedly supplying ammunition illegally. Both suspects have been charged to court, according to the CP. On child trafficking, Afolabi said police operatives rescued 10 children during the period under review and reunited them with their families. He specifically disclosed that two suspects, including a 38-year-old , were arrested on October 11 over the alleged stealing of two children, seven-year-old Chiamaka Chikeze and nine-month-old Goodluck Chikeze. The children were reportedly recovered and handed back to their parents, while the suspects were charged to court. The police boss also announced the arrest of a five-man vehicle theft syndicate, aged 43, and 40. A Toyota Corolla with registration number ROU 9338J was recovered from the suspects, who have also been charged to court. In another operation, two suspected cultists, aged 27, and 25, were arrested on October 31 for allegedly dispossessing students of Abia State University, Uturu, of their mobile phones and other valuables at gunpoint. A locally fabricated firearm was recovered from them. The CP said one of the suspects had confessed to belonging to the Black Axe Confraternity, adding that efforts were ongoing to apprehend other members of the gang. nigeria.description: By Sola Ogundipe What if the chemical produced in abundance by cancer cells could be turned against the cancers? What if, instead of flooding the entire body with powerful drugs in an attempt to destroy a tumour, scientists could persuade cancer cells to manufacture destructive chemicals from within? That possibility is at the centre of an intriguing scientific breakthrough in Japan, where researchers have developed an experimental technique that exploits carbon monoxide produced by cancer cells to generate cancer-killing compounds inside them. The approach turns an unusual feature of cancer biology into a potential therapeutic advantage. Rather than administering an already manufactured toxic drug that circulates through the body and can damage healthy tissues, the researchers have devised a chemical system that produces an anticancer compound inside targeted cancer cells. In laboratory experiments, the technique successfully generated toxic compounds in several cancer cell lines while leaving a noncancerous cell line without detectable production of the same compound. Although still at an early experimental stage, the findings could open a new direction in cancer treatment, particularly in the long-standing search for ways to destroy malignant cells while sparing healthy tissues from the collateral damage associated with conventional chemotherapy. The research, led by Katsunori Tanaka at the RIKEN Pioneering Research Institute (PRI), Japan, was published in Nature Communications. Cancer treatment has long been complicated by a fundamental problem: drugs powerful enough to destroy malignant cells can also injure normal cells. Chemotherapy, for instance, often affects healthy tissues because many anticancer medicines cannot distinguish perfectly between cancerous and noncancerous cells. The resulting damage can produce debilitating side effects, including nausea, fatigue, hair loss and suppression of the immune system. Scientists have consequently been exploring more selective ways of delivering or generating anticancer agents at the precise location where they are needed. Tanaka and colleagues focused on carbon monoxide, a gas commonly recognised for its toxicity but also naturally produced in small quantities in the human body. Their strategy was to deliver a metal-based catalyst into cells and use the available carbon monoxide as the chemical fuel for a reaction that manufactures an anticancer substance. In principle, the reaction would be activated predominantly in cancer cells, where sufficient carbon monoxide is available, rather than in healthy tissues. The research represents part of a developing scientific field known as therapeutic in vivo synthetic chemistry, which seeks to use chemical reactions inside living organisms to manufacture therapeutic substances where they are needed. nigeria.title: Nigeria is losing $1.6bn yearly to avoidable blindness — Aghaji
nigeria.description: By Prisca Sam-Duru Almost on a daily basis, across Nigeria and much of Africa, millions of people wake up to a world they cannot see clearly. A farmer peeks at his cassava farms for instance, but cannot differentiate the difference between weed and crop. A trader holds her register at arm’s length, guessing at figures she once read at a glance. A child in the back row of a classroom copies from a board that is almost a blur. More often, an old woman needs her grandchild to lead her to the market because the road she walked for over 50 years has become unrecognizable. Those are not statistics. They are the human face of a crisis that Africa has lived with for too long. As Professor Ada Aghaji told a packed hall at the University of Nigeria on October 29, 2026, this is a crisis Africa can no longer afford to ignore. Delivering the institution’s 254th Inaugural Lecture, titled “Let There Be Sight: Building Sustainable Eye Health Systems for All in Africa,” Aghaji, Professor of Ophthalmology and Eye Health Systems, made a simple but very powerful argument: eye health in Africa is not just a medical issue. It is an economic issue. A development issue. A justice issue. And the numbers prove it. According to her, Nigeria loses an estimated $1.6 billion every year in productivity because of vision impairment. Across Africa, the loss is about $9 billion. Globally, it stands at a staggering $410 billion. Behind those figures are livelihoods cut short, schooling interrupted, and families pushed deeper into poverty. Yet, as Aghaji stressed, much of this vision loss can be prevented or treated. A pair of spectacles costing less than a bag of rice. A 15-minute cataract operation. A routine screening at a primary health centre. Why, then, do millions of Africans continue to live with avoidable blindness when the solutions already exist? That was the question at the heart of her lecture. Two Children, Two Worlds Perhaps the most haunting moment of the lecture came not from statistics, but from a story. Aghaji spoke of two children born with congenital rubella syndrome; a condition that can cause cataracts, deafness and other disabilities. One was born in Nigeria. He faced delays, barriers to treatment and rehabilitation, and ended up blind. The other was a Somali refugee child in England. He received timely surgery, spectacles and hearing aids, and with them, a chance to learn, to play, to grow Their medical conditions were similar. Their opportunities were profoundly different. The contrast, Aghaji argued, is the story of Africa’s eye health system in miniature. Medical knowledge alone does not guarantee care. What determines whether a child sees or goes blind is often not the disease, but the system around it: whether there is money to pay, a health worker to detect the problem, a referral that works, a hospital that can be reached. nigeria.title: Naira would’ve been worthless, moved with wheelbarrow if we didn’t act – Tinubu
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu said that Naira would have been so worthless, it would be moved about by wheelbarrow if not for his economic policies that moved Nigeria away from the brink of financial collapse. Read Also: Tinubu to Nigerians: ‘I promise better future’ Tinubu, the presidential candidate of All Progressives Congress, APC, said this during his visit to Akwa Ibom State, where he urged voters to support his administration and Governor Umo Eno. He described the January 16, 2027 election as consequential, saying it would determine the country’s direction. Defending his economic policies, Tinubu said his administration had moved Nigeria away from the brink of financial collapse. According to him, “This coming election, on January 16th is a consequential election. It will define the direction of this country. “When I took over, 27 governors out of 36 of this country were unable to pay salary, not to talk of pension, and gratuity. Today, I can say that we are out of that tunnel. “And I can beat my chest to say we are out of the despair, the dark tunnel of uncertainty and the calamity of a possible bankruptcy. “By now if we didn’t take over, if we didn’t do what we did, we will be using the wheelbarrows to move our naira about because it will have become valueless.” On young voters The President urged the electorate, particularly young people, to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs. He described it as their most potent instrument for determining the country’s political future. At a reception held in his honour at Ibom Palm Resort, Tinubu praised Eno. He described the resort as evidence of purposeful leadership and the possibility of reclaiming environmentally degraded land for productive use. “We are standing on a resort to the glory of God. It is a product of 73 acres of land of gully erosion, reclaimed, surrounded with a good, romantic, artificial lake, demonstrating a serious vision that is achievable when honest people are working for their homes,” he said. nigeria.title: ADC Crisis: What becomes of Atiku, Mark, Gombe if Supreme Court decides party’s fate?
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress (ADC) was meant to be the meeting point of opposition forces determined to challenge President Bola Tinubu in 2027. Instead, the party has become the battleground for a struggle that could undo the coalition it was expected to accommodate. Read Also: Court sacks Mark-led ADC exco, voids Atiku’s candidacy Barely 24 hours after former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar took his presidential campaign to Sokoto, a Federal High Court judgment delivered by Justice Peter Lifu threw the party into fresh uncertainty, nullifying the David Mark-led leadership and decisions taken under it, including the process that produced Atiku as presidential candidate. For Mark and his allies, it was a setback at a critical moment. For Nafiu Bala Gombe, who challenged the leadership transition, it was a victory in a battle he had refused to abandon. For Atiku, it was a reminder that the platform on which he hopes to return to Aso Rock may not be entirely within his control. With the Mark faction preparing to appeal, attention is shifting to the appellate courts. Whatever the eventual outcome, the political fortunes of some of the coalition’s most prominent figures are at stake. How it all began The dispute began when former ADC National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu, facilitated a leadership transition that brought Mark and former Osun State Governor, Rauf Aregbesola, into the party as National Chairman and National Secretary respectively. The arrangement offered opposition politicians an existing political structure around which to build a challenge to the APC. But Gombe, a former Deputy National Chairman, North, objected, arguing that the party’s constitution provided a succession procedure that was not followed. His challenge produced Justice Lifu’s November 5 judgment. The Mark faction, however, insists that the leadership question had already been examined by the court. It points to the July 2, 2026, judgment of Justice Musa Liman in a separate suit instituted by House of Representatives member Leke Abejide. Justice Liman upheld preliminary objections, including lack of jurisdiction, standing and failure to exhaust internal party remedies. He also made findings favourable to the defendants concerning the leadership transition The Mark camp argues that a court of coordinate jurisdiction cannot overturn another court’s decision. However, the different plaintiffs and the precise issues and reliefs sought in the two cases make the legal relationship between the judgments a matter requiring highest judicial determination. The Supreme Court had intervened on April 30, setting aside an earlier status quo ante bellum order and directing an expedited hearing at the Federal High Court. nigeria.title: CBN updates guidelines for stablecoins operation
nigeria.description: •Sets N15bn capital requirement By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Central Bank of Nigeria has issued guidelines for virtual asset providers in the country, setting minimum capital requirement of N10 billion and N15 billion for Classes 1 and 2 issuers, respectively. This was contained in a circular with reference number PSP/DIR/PUB/CIR/001/004, date November 5, 2026 and signed by the Director of Payments Systems Policy, Mr. Musa Jimoh. According to the bank, “A Class 1 Licensed Issuer shall maintain paid-up capital of N10 billion Naira or such higher amount as the Bank may prescribe, on entry and at all times thereafter. Class 2 Licensed Issuer shall maintain minimum paid-up capital of N15 billion or such higher amount as the Bank may prescribe, on entry and at all times thereafter. “Both classes shall comply with the capital deposit and corresponding evidence and supplementary requirements in Section 17. There is no offshore issuer exemption from incorporation, licensing or capital.” Class 2 stablecoins are digital tokens designed to maintain a stable value against foreign currencies, including the US dollar, while Class 1 refers to issuers of naira-referenced stablecoins. CBN said the emergence of virtual assets, stablecoins, and tokenised payment instruments “presents significant opportunities for innovation in payments, remittances, settlement, and digital commerce,” but that, “their growing adoption also introduces risks relating to financial stability, monetary policy, consumer protection, illicit finance, operational resilience, and foreign exchange management.” It added that the guidelines were issued pursuant to its statutory mandate to promote monetary and financial stability and regulate Nigeria’s payments system. “These Guidelines establish a risk-based framework for the licensing, regulation, supervision, and oversight of Non-Security Virtual Assets, including stablecoins, Deposit Money Tokens (DMTs), and related Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs). “These Guidelines seek to support responsible innovation while safeguarding the integrity, stability, and efficiency of the Nigerian financial system. “These Guidelines also seek to provide regulatory requirements relating to governance, prudential standards, consumer protection, operational resilience, AML/CFT/CPF compliance, and reporting obligations for entities and persons engaged in regulated non-security virtual asset activities within or involving Nigeria,” the bank explained. The CBN’s updated framework outlines clear boundaries for Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs), with a sharp focus on foreign exchange liquidity, consumer protection, and peer-to-peer (P2P) trading identity protocols. Curbing money laundering The guidelines place great responsibilities on issuers to ensure that their activities do not aid money laundering or terrorism financing, as they are required to provide detailed data on their customers. nigeria.title: Supreme Court Justices placed on US visa ban – Retiring jurist
nigeria.description: •Judgement that gave Uzodimma governorship victory fingered By Ikechukwu Nnochiri A retiring Justice of the Supreme Court, Justice Uwani Abba-Aji, disclosed on Friday that some justices of the court had been placed on a visa ban by the United States of America. Read Also : Uzodinma sworn-in as sixth governor of Imo Justice Abba-Aji, speaking during a valedictory session held to mark her retirement from the bench, said the travel ban followed a judgment of the apex court that she described as widely misinterpreted. She said: “My time on the Supreme Court bench was filled with challenges, some of which have served as additional opportunities to stand firm on the side of justice, regardless of the consequences. “One of such challenging judgments was widely misinterpreted and led to a travel ban to the United States of America being imposed on all members of the panel, a ban which still holds today.” Even though Justice Abba-Aji did not mention the specific case that led to the imposition of a US visa ban on Supreme Court Justices, Vanguard understands that it was connected to the legal tussle that followed the 2019 governorship election in Imo State. A seven-member panel of the Supreme Court, which included the current Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, and Justice Abba-Aji, had on January 14, 2020, nullified the election of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Emeka Ihedioha, and ordered the swearing-in of the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Hope Uzodimma, who had initially finished fourth in the governorship election. In the lead judgment delivered by the CJN, the apex court ordered the immediate withdrawal of the Certificate of Return that had already been issued to Ihedioha by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). It ordered that a fresh Certificate of Return be issued to Uzodimma as the validly elected governor of Imo State. To arrive at the decision, the apex court panel vacated the concurrent verdicts of both the Court of Appeal and the Imo State Governorship Election Petitions Tribunal, which had earlier affirmed the PDP candidate as winner of the gubernatorial contest. Votes counted in courtroom The panel went ahead to add election results from 388 polling units, amounting to 213,295 votes, which were tendered before the tribunal by a police officer who testified as PW-54, but which INEC disowned. After all the votes were computed inside the courtroom, Uzodimma was declared the candidate who secured the majority of lawful votes cast at the election, a judgment that elicited wide reactions and protests. Other members of the panel, which was led by the then CJN, Justice Tanko Muhammad, were Justices Sylvester Ngwuta, Kayode Ariwola and Amiru Sanusi. nigeria.title: Mutfwang: Educated Nigerians masterminding corruption, institutional decay
nigeria.description: …says professionals behind major governance failures …challenges graduates to choose integrity over wealth By Joseph Erunke, Abuja Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has accused educated Nigerians of masterminding some of the country’s most damaging corruption scandals, financial fraud and institutional abuses, saying the nation’s governance crisis is not a result of a shortage of intellectual capacity but a failure of conscience. Mutfwang said some of the most sophisticated acts of financial fraud, contract manipulation, money laundering and subversion of public institutions were perpetrated by people whose academic qualifications and professional expertise should ordinarily be deployed for national development. The governor spoke on Friday in Abuja while delivering the convocation lecture at the 15th Convocation Ceremony of Veritas University. In his lecture titled, “Building the Nigeria We Want: The Role of the Educated Mind,” he warned that education without moral discipline had become a dangerous instrument against the country’s progress. He challenged the graduating students to rethink the purpose of university education, insisting that academic certificates and intellectual brilliance would amount to little if deployed for selfish interests at the expense of society. According to him, Nigeria’s development challenges cannot be blamed entirely on inadequate manpower or lack of expertise, as many individuals responsible for undermining public institutions are highly educated and professionally trained. Describing the situation as an uncomfortable reality the country must confront, Mutfwang said some of Nigeria’s most entrenched governance failures were products of educated minds. He said: “Indeed, I make an uncomfortable observation: the afflictions I diagnosed earlier, prebendalism, the privatisation of public office, grand corruption, the capture of institutions, are almost never the work of illiterate minds. They are overwhelmingly executed by educated minds. “The contract, the doctored account, the laundered fund, the ingenious evasion of law. All these are the signatures of trained minds. This is the paradox we must confront. The educated mind is at once our greatest hope, and when corrupted, it becomes our most sophisticated danger.” The governor also cited internet fraudsters, popularly known as Yahoo boys, as an example of intelligence deployed in the wrong direction, arguing that criminal ingenuity reflected a lack of moral restraint rather than an absence of intelligence. “The Yahoo boy is certainly not a derelict. He is a work of intelligence, but intelligence wrongly applied,” he said. Mutfwang maintained that Nigeria had no shortage of brilliant citizens, noting the achievements of Nigerians across different professions and on international platforms. nigeria.title: 2027: APGA adopts Tinubu, flags off nationwide campaign
nigeria.description: …Soludo cites South-East projects, urges strategic voting By Steve Oko The All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) has adopted President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate for the 2027 general election, with Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, saying the decision was informed by the need for progressive forces to work together. Soludo made the declaration on Friday while flagging off APGA’s nationwide election campaign at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, Anambra State, where the party unveiled more than 253 candidates contesting various elective positions across the country. The governor, who is APGA’s National Leader, said the decision to support Tinubu was consistent with the party’s political tradition, recalling that APGA had similarly adopted former President Goodluck Jonathan in the 2011 and 2015 presidential elections. He said the party’s support for Tinubu was also informed by what he described as the Federal Government’s commitment to the South-East, particularly in infrastructure development. “Today, as we unveil our campaign as the foremost progressive party in Nigeria, we are also officially adopting President Bola Tinubu as the presidential candidate of APGA. “We did it in 2011 and 2015 for President Jonathan. We are repeating it in 2027 because progressives are working together to support a President who loves Ndi Igbo and Ndi Anambra,” Soludo declared. Citing the dualisation and rehabilitation of the Enugu-Onitsha Expressway and other federal projects in the region, the governor urged voters to approach the 2027 elections with political pragmatism rather than sentiment. He said voting decisions should be guided by tangible benefits, enlightened self-interest and strategic political considerations capable of advancing the interests of the South-East. Soludo also charged APGA candidates and members to intensify grassroots mobilisation through door-to-door campaigns, assuring them that he would personally join the candidates in soliciting votes. He expressed confidence in the party’s electoral prospects, urging voters to distinguish between reason and emotion ahead of the January 16 and February 6, 2027 elections. At the event, Soludo presented party flags to 44 APGA candidates contesting legislative seats in Anambra State. The candidates comprised three senatorial candidates, 11 House of Representatives candidates and 30 State House of Assembly candidates. Earlier, APGA National Chairman, Barrister Sly Ezeokenwa, commended Soludo for what he described as transparent and competitive party primaries conducted in compliance with electoral laws. Ezeokenwa attributed the influx of new members into the party to Soludo’s people-oriented policies, describing Anambra as APGA’s political stronghold. He expressed confidence that the party would record a decisive victory in the forthcoming elections. nigeria.title: 2027: Ebonyi youths march against political violence, intimidation
nigeria.description: …demand peaceful campaigns, protection of opposition parties By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki A group under the aegis of Concerned Ebonyi Youth for Democracy has staged a peaceful road march in Ebonyi State to protest alleged political violence, harassment and intimidation of opposition political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group condemned reported attacks and killings of opposition party members in parts of the state, insisting that all political parties must be allowed to campaign and exercise their democratic rights without fear. Addressing participants during the march, Nollywood actor, Steve Rostick Eze, said the demonstration was aimed at promoting peaceful campaigns and elections while condemning attacks on opposition parties. He urged youths to shun violence and mobilise voters to support candidates of their choice without fear, favour or intimidation. Eze also called on security agencies to provide adequate protection for all political parties and ensure compliance with electoral rules and the rule of law. “We have gathered today to march for peace, march for freedom, march for democracy. It is time that we say no to violence. It is time that we say no to oppression. It is time for us to take back peace, freedom in our state, Ebonyi State,” he said. The National President of Anyigaemeya Youth Assembly, Mr. Nnanna Nwangene, also condemned political intimidation and thuggery, declaring his support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid and the governorship ambition of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Dr. Ifeanyichukwu Odii, in 2027. Nwangene said the march was to demonstrate that Ebonyi belonged to all political parties and that citizens had the constitutional right to freely express their political preferences. He said: “We have gathered to tell the whole world and the Ebonyians that Ebonyi belongs to all of us. Ebonyi is not a one-party state. Ebonyi belongs to all political parties. “We want a freedom where all political parties will be allowed to participate in a peaceful campaign without being attacked. We want every Ebonyian to understand that we are marching for peace.” He called on opposition parties to be allowed to exercise their political rights without harassment, adding that political differences should not lead to violence. Another youth leader, Prince Igwe Udemanta, warned against a recurrence of election-related violence in the state, recalling the loss of lives during previous election cycles, particularly in 2003 and 2007. He said Ebonyi should not become a state associated with bloodshed, stressing that political disagreements must not degenerate into violence. Udemanta urged supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), APGA and other political parties to conduct their activities peacefully. nigeria.title: CAFA urges unified policies to grow Africa’s fashion economy to $500bn
nigeria.description: By Benjamin Njoku The Confederation of African Fashion,CAFA, has called on African countries to harmonise their fashion policies, strengthen intellectual property protection and invest in local manufacturing as part of efforts to grow the continent’s fashion economy to $500 billion. The President of CAFA, Professor Lai Labode, made the call during the unveiling of the joint stand of the organisation and the Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy at the ongoing CANEX WKND 2026. Labode said Africa had no shortage of creative talent but lacked the structures and policies needed to translate its creative potential into economic value. “In Africa, we don’t have a shortage of talent. What Africa needs is structure. Money always follows structure,” he said. He said the African Fashion Industry Growth Charter, developed by CAFA, was built around 10 pillars designed to address challenges across the fashion value chain, including policy harmonisation, raw material cultivation and processing, intellectual property protection, counterfeiting, logistics and market access. Labode stressed the need for African countries to process their raw materials locally instead of exporting them in largely unprocessed forms, arguing that local value addition would create jobs and retain more wealth within the continent. Using cotton production as an example, he compared Brazil’s reported $5.3 billion cotton exports with China’s earnings from cotton production and processing, saying Africa needed to build its own processing capacity to compete more effectively. He also identified intellectual property protection as a major priority, noting that African designers and creative businesses needed stronger systems to protect their original works from counterfeiting and unauthorised use. On market access, Labode disclosed plans to establish about 10 African fashion houses across the continent, alongside outlets in New York, Paris, Milan and London, to promote African designers and connect them with international markets. He called for common intellectual property rules and standards across African countries, warning that fragmented systems could weaken the continent’s competitiveness. The CAFA president also urged member states to support the intellectual property framework under the African Continental Free Trade Area, saying the relevant protocol annexes had been passed in February 2026 but required wider participation by African countries. Speaking in the same vein, the Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musa Musawa, identified private-sector partnerships, policy development and infrastructure as essential to strengthening Nigeria’s fashion industry. Musawa said the collaboration with CAFA should translate into tangible economic benefits, particularly job creation, while promoting African unity, cultural pride and soft power. nigeria.title: CANEX WKND 2026 lights up Lagos as Davido, Fally Ipupa, Flavour headline star-studded concert tonight
nigeria.description: By Benjamin Njoku & Tony-Okafor Favour The 2026 edition of Creative Africa Nexus Weekend, CANEX WKND, which opened at the Professor Wole Soyinka Arts Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos on Thursday, continues this evening with a blockbuster concert. Headlining the night are some of Africa’s biggest music stars, including Nigeria’s Davido, Congolese sensation Fally Ipupa, Flavour, Cali-Ber Tha Grime, Sabrina Francis and Nigerian DJ duo Wanni X Handi. The concert will bring together performers from Africa and the Caribbean for an evening of live music, rhythm and cultural celebration. The four-day gathering, themed “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World”, has brought the once moribund Arts Theatre back to life. It convened leading voices from film, music, fashion, sport, publishing, gastronomy and business to advance trade, investment and commercial opportunities across Africa’s creative economy. The opening day featured a series of masterclasses and sessions, including Building Your Brand as an Independent Artist, Podcasting for Success, Fashion Masterclass: Building Profitable Fashion Brands, and Building Sustainable Business Models in the Performing Arts. In attendance were Vice-President Kassim Shettima, Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Afreximbank President and Chairman of the Board of Directors, Dr George Elombi; Nigeria’s Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole; and African Continental Free Trade Area Secretary-General, Wamkele Mene. Other dignitaries included the Minister of Arts, Culture, Tourism, and the Creative Economy for Nigeria, Hon Hannatu Musa Musawa; Mrs Kanayo Awani, Executive Vice President of Intra-African Trade and Export Development at Afreximbank; Hon Ginger Moxey, Minister for Grand Bahama; Emmy Award-winning actor Uzo Aduba; filmmaker Funke Akindele; and actors Richard Mofe-Damijo and Thuso Mbedu among other dignitaries. Speaking while declaring the programme open, Shettima said the world will eventually hear about the can-do spirit of African women. He commended Afreximbank for committing $2 billion to Africa’s creative industries by 2027, noting that the industry is not just about entertainment, but also serious economic infrastructure. Shettima took the audience down memory lane, recalling almost 50 years ago when the same Arts Theatre hosted the second World Black and African Festival of Arts and Culture, FESTAC ’77, where the Black World declared through music, dance, literature and art that “our culture was not just a footnote to history, but the very core within it. “In 1977, we came to celebrate our culture. In 2024, we are here to capitalize it,” he said. He urged Africans to be proud of who they are without asking for anything in return. nigeria.title: Ebonyi Youths Protest Political Violence, Intimidation Ahead Of 2027 Elections
nigeria.description: Hundreds of youths in Ebonyi State have staged a peaceful march through Abakaliki, the state capital, calling for an end to political violence, intimidation and harassment of opposition members ahead of the 2027 general elections. The protesters, under the aegis of Concerned Ebonyi Youth for Democracy, said they came from the 13 local government areas of the state to demand a peaceful political atmosphere in which all citizens can participate without fear. The demonstrators marched through major streets in Abakaliki, displaying placards with messages including, “Democracy Needs Peaceful Ideas, Not Weapons” and “Protect Freedom of Speech in Ebonyi.” Addressing journalists during the rally, a spokesperson for the group said the youths would not accept any attempt to undermine their constitutional rights. “Our constitutional rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly are not negotiable,” the spokesperson said. The group also expressed concern over reported incidents of physical violence, harassment and voter intimidation targeting opposition figures in parts of the state. “We will not sit by while political thuggery and intimidation threaten to ruin our state’s democratic process. Every citizen, regardless of party alignment, deserves to participate without fear for their safety,” the spokesperson added. FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign Friday for Aaron van Wirdum’s The Genesis Book , offering a redesigned Collectors Edition limited to 333 hand-signed, individually numbered hardcovers in an exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Each Collectors Edition hardcover is hand-signed and hand-numbered by van Wirdum, the former Bitcoin Magazine editor-in-chief whose book traces the people, projects and ideas that preceded Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer cash design. The standard package is priced at $221 and pairs the book with a limited trading card carrying a Certificate of Authenticity, a collector pin, a sticker sheet, the slipcase and a digital package. Two one-of-one packages sit outside the ordinary number queue. The #1 package is listed at $5,000 and the #21 package at $2,500; each includes the matching numbered copy, a matching one-of-one collector card and the same accessories as the standard collector package. Standard collector numbers are assigned in purchase order starting at #2 and skipping #21, the campaign FAQ says. Once preorders close, the signed Genesis print run will not be reproduced. The Genesis Book Collector's Edition is live! 333 copies. Individually numbered. Exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Hand-signed by Aaron van Wirdum. Once they're gone, they're gone. pic.twitter.com/BgiJoCVt8m — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What ships with the anniversary editions Beside the signed run, Bitcoin Magazine Books is selling a Premium Edition hardcover for $160 with foil stamping, a ribbon marker, stained page edges and custom endsheets. That edition is not limited, signed, numbered or slipcased, and it does not include the collector accessories or digital files. A standalone Digital Package at $9.99 delivers the ebook in EPUB and the audiobook in MP4 immediately after purchase, independent of whether the physical campaign clears its funding bar. Physical collector and premium orders are scheduled to ship in calendar year 2027. Van Wirdum , who discovered bitcoin in 2013 and later led Bitcoin Magazine ‘s editorial desk, frames The Genesis Book as a history of computer scientists, privacy activists and heterodox economists who chased government-independent digital money long before the 2008 white paper — from early cypherpunk culture through experiments such as David Chaum’s ecash, Wei Dai’s b-money, Adam Back’s Hashcash and Hal Finney’s reusable proof of work. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission filed a criminal complaint Thursday against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, alleging it ran an unlicensed digital-asset exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025, and notified the government to block the platform from Dec. 5. The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026. From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok. That conduct amounts to operating a digital-asset exchange under Section 3 of the Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018) without a license, a violation of Section 26 punishable under Section 66, the SEC said. The case now moves to an inquiry official, then prosecutors and the courts. Separately, the SEC submitted Bitget’s website, other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society under a 2025 royal decree that authorizes access blocks on unlicensed trading platforms. From Dec. 5, the public “will be unable to access the platform,” the statement said, and investors still holding assets there were told to consider acting before the cutoff. A licensed path that now sits next to a criminal case The enforcement push lands weeks after Bitget announced a planned acquisition of GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics (Thailand), a Bangkok digital-asset exchange and brokerage that already holds Thai licenses, through its interest in BTGT Management (Thailand) Ltd. Under that deal, GMO Internet and its Thai holding company would transfer their entire stake in GMO-Z — about 49% and 50.94%, respectively — to BTGT or a designee at completion, a Sept. 24 GMO Internet filing showed. Bitget said completion remains subject to regulatory approval and, after a change-of-control nod, it intends to introduce its trading platform to Thai users under local rules. “Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations,” Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said in the Oct. 20 release. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky, her Spring/Summer 2027 collection , Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis. The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A Cycle Of Giving Back In nature, nothing is wasted and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back.That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. Show And Availability Earth & Sky will be presented on November 11, 2026, and will be available from December 2026 at the Banke Kuku flagship on Victoria Island, Lagos, and through global stockists. entertainment.title: FinTribe Finance Fair 2026: Empowers Over 10,000 Women to Build Wealth and Financial Independence
entertainment.description: Over 10,000 women gathered at the Landmark Event Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, on October 31, 2026, for the fourth edition of FinTribe Finance Fair , a growing movement dedicated to helping African women move from financial awareness to wealth creation and ownership. Themed I CAN and powered by returning lead sponsor Sycamore, the event brought together financial experts, business leaders, entrepreneurs and influential personalities, including Funke Akindele , Omoni Oboli , BamBam , Sola Adesakin and Olufemi Shobanjo , for a day of practical financial education, inspiring conversations and meaningful opportunities. For FinTribe founder Jennifer Awirigwe , popularly known as Financial Jennifer, the fair represents a bigger mission: helping women gain the confidence and resources to take charge of their financial futures. “Financial education is important, but knowledge must eventually become action. We want women to leave Finance Fair knowing that they can save, invest, grow their income, build businesses and take ownership of their financial future,” she shared ahead of the event. Beyond Finance Fair, FinTribe is building a community where women learn about money and put that knowledge into practice . With a presence across 43 countries, the organisation has reached over 20,000 women through financial education, supported more than 5,000 women with capital market training and helped members collectively save and invest millions of dollars. Through its Wealth Builders Academy, savings and investment community, real estate initiatives and recently launched FinTribe App, the organisation continues to create opportunities for women to build healthier financial habits, develop investment confidence and work towards long-term financial independence. At the fair, award-winning filmmaker Omoni Oboli encouraged women to pursue their ambitions without neglecting their wellbeing, reminding them to take things one step at a time, prioritise rest and ask for help when needed. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.” The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally. The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. Bringing Prince Gyasi into the collaboration introduces another creative perspective, connecting music and contemporary African art through a shared celebration of African expression. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. A UK-based social worker and parent of children with disabilities, Helen founded OBIMI to support families and challenge disability stigma.
